A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POCDETECT and POCTRACE study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–G are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original token interpretation/repetition experiments, vocabulary analyses, and corpus-pollution estimation results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–6, with supporting appendix material.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and data analyses, including their numerical results and appendix evidence.

M1.justification: POCDETECT retains GLM-4-32B fine-tuning with expert labels and search context. POCTRACE retains the same token-ID regression, frequency bounds, and pollution-estimation procedure (Sections 4–5 and Appendix C).

E1.justification: The evaluated Chinese token tasks and corpus coverage remain unchanged, including mC4, Pile, C4, Dolma, ROOTS, and CommonCrawl material. The new GPT-5/GPT-oss footnote does not document additional datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The model comparison sets in Tables 1–2 are unchanged. No evaluated baseline or comparison method is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: The prompts, DeepSeek-V3 judging, exact-match evaluation, 3,920-sample dataset with an 8:2 split, and corpus-mixing settings are retained. No additional evaluation protocol accompanies the GPT-5/GPT-oss footnote.

E4.justification: The cross-corpus transfer analysis, mixture-ratio verification, GPT output examples, and Appendix E–G case studies and distribution analyses are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: The quantile choices and empirical-bound reporting remain unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test.

E6.justification: V2 adds the qualitative assertion that the polluted-vocabulary observation also applies to GPT-5 and GPT-oss, without accompanying measurements. Existing numerical results and illustrated cases are unchanged; for example, the mC4 estimate remains 3.13% against 2.14% ground truth.

T1.justification: The definitions, Equations 1–5, substring-frequency bounds, and illustrative proof using the corpus 'ab ab' are retained. Quotation-mark corrections in the proof do not change its mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: Abstract footnote 1 extends the polluted-vocabulary claim to GPT-5 and GPT-oss. The principal contributions and the approximately 0.5% GPT-4o content speculation retain their earlier meaning and scope.

C2.justification: The explanations of token behavior, corpus-transfer differences, and imbalanced pollution categories are unchanged. Both versions retain the lack of GPT-4o training-data ground truth and the restriction to Chinese as limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly reports annotator pay of six dollars per hour. The access note changes from an explicit code-release statement at pollutedtokens.site to a project website at pollutedtokens.github.io. The PDFs do not establish whether actual code availability changed.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to abnormal-token research and tokenizer-based corpus inference are unchanged. Reference reflow and footnote renumbering introduce no new research positioning.

P1.justification: V2 updates author affiliations, adds an Acknowledgements section and the abstract footnote, and makes limited wording corrections, particularly in Appendix A.2. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All 16 figures and 10 tables are retained with the same substantive content. Local spacing, typography, and positioning change, including Table 2 and the reflow around affiliations, footnotes, and acknowledgements.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves reporting transparency by disclosing annotator compensation in Appendix A.2 and identifying funding and institutional support. These are limited gains: the scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and the GPT-5/GPT-oss extension adds no separate validation.
